ops.title: content-over-RPC shared holder shipped; cc-pool pure-Go consumer. RESOLVED 2026-07-02: full LIVE re-fuse DONE — all 6 pool accounts on nfs, zero panic (mitigations validated live). Required two fixes: v0.36.1 (mcp-needs-auth-cache private) + v0.36.2 (convert identity verify reads backing file, not through the mount, else --force stalls on a busy dir)

ops.body:
**Shipped fusekit v0.18.0 (2026-06-25, main @ f302a7b)** — Phase 3A of the shared multi-tenant holder. See [[fusekit-global-holder-direction]] for the end goal, [[claude-pool-holder-kill-meltdown]] / [[fusekit-holder-fork-bomb-incident]] for why the shared holder exists.

What landed:
- **`content` package** is the neutral home for BOTH the consumer seam (`Source`/`Tree`/`Entry`/`EntryKind`) AND the bridge wire (`BridgeServer`/`BridgeClient`/ops). Lifted out of `fileproviderd`, which keeps source-compat aliases. So the fuse holder imports `content`, never the File-Provider package. Added read-side Tree ops (Stat/List/ReadAt/Readlink) + `ErrClass`/`ClassedError` for a fully-remote consumer (cc-notes, Phase 4); additive, `BridgeProtoVersion` stays 1.
- **`holderfs`** (darwin-only, `//go:build fuse && cgo && darwin`) is the generic content FS: passthrough mirror of Base + live-symlink carve-outs + PrivateRoot redirects (incl. atomic-write temp **prefixes** via `MountSpec.PrivatePrefixes`) + synth entries. The two cc-pool views (claudeJSON + settings) collapse into ONE generic `synthView` because the merge/inject now live consumer-side over RPC. `synth.go` is build-tag-FREE (pure) so the off-handler/write-through/drain logic is unit-tested without a `-tags fuse` run.
- **Load-bearing invariant**: synth READS serve a holder-side cache refreshed OFF the fuse handler path (`currentBytes` only stats local `Entry.Freshness` files + maybe spawns a goroutine; the bridge RPC is `refreshOnce` on a worker). A hung consumer is stale-but-served, never a parked fuse-t worker. Synth WRITES passthrough to a durable local file then schedule a background write-through RPC; drained before teardown (`Flusher`/`Drainer`, `drainGrace=6s` > the 5.5s bridge RPC ceiling).
- **`fusekit.MountSpec`** + `MountSet.Build(spec) (Config, error)`; `mountd.Request` content fields; `Host.Setup(spec)`; `Client.AddMount`/`RemoteHost.AddMount`. `cmd/holder` serves `holderfs.Host()`; dead `PassthroughHost` removed.
- **Fail-loud**: `holderfs.Build` errors when content is wired but the consumer bridge is unreachable — a bare passthrough would serve cc-pool the raw `~/.claude.json` and route writes into plain claude's shared state (the HIGH finding from the adversarial review). `ContentMode` is read and fails loud on the unimplemented "tree" mode.

**Phase 3B SHIPPED (cc-pool cutover, 2026-06-26) — consumes fusekit v0.19.0.** cc-pool stopped self-exec'ing its own binary as the in-process holder and became a **pure-Go** consumer driving the shared, signed, multi-tenant `fusekit-holder` over RPC. Net diff ~980 insertions / ~6900 deletions.
- **fusekit v0.19.0** (additive): `overlay.HolderSpec` gained `BridgeSocket`/`ContentMode`/`ProbePath`/`PrivatePrefixes`; `RemoteFuseProvider.Setup` builds a `MountSpec` + `AddMount` (the fuse arm became content-aware like the FP arm) — so cc-pool's safety-critical heal path is UNCHANGED, content just rides along. `Select`'s gate now accepts a cask `ExecPath` (`holderCanSpawn` = ExecPath set OR `fusekit.Built()`), so a pure build drives the cask holder. **Bug fixed:** holderfs probe was 4 KiB but cc-pool's deep-probe (`overlay.ProbeFileSize`) requires exactly 2 MiB — every live mount read as wedged → spurious symlink retreats; restored to 2 MiB (a wire contract; the size is load-bearing for multi-RPC wedge detection). Caught a self-referential `replace` accidentally added to fusekit's OWN go.mod before tagging — removed it.
- **cc-pool**: new `overlay.PoolContentSource` (`content.Source`) serves the merged `.claude.json` + injected `settings.json` over the daemon's `content.BridgeServer`; merge/split/inject/classify + `writeThroughMu` preserved (tested). Deleted: the in-process mirror (`internal/overlay/fuse*.go`), `holderpolicy.go`, the `proc.Supervisor` arm of `holder.go`, `SpawnHolder`, the `mount-holder` subcommand, `MountsSocketPath`/`HolderBinDir`, `HolderStatus.Skewed`/`SpawnError`. Kept the per-row heal net (`retryUnvouchedFuseRows` + breakers + symlink-retreat + deep-probe). `holderClient()` Owner-scoped to "cc-pool" (multi-tenant); `ccp service uninstall` now `Reclaim`s only cc-pool's mounts (NEVER shuts down/kills the shared holder — cc-notes may use it); `ccp fuse enable` installs the holder cask. The heal ticker (`healFuseRows`) replaced the supervisor; capability = cask-installed-or-reachable (NOT `fusekit.Built()`).
- **DEFERRED (no cruft):** `OwnerSessions` control endpoint — no 3B caller (the heal loop already session-gates via `procscan.CountByConfigDir`). docs/Formula `-tags fuse` cleanup → final-cleanup task. **NOT shippable to users yet:** a cc-pool release would make fuse users try to use the unpublished cask → silent symlink downgrade, so the cc-pool release is gated on the cask publishing (signing secrets, below). Live re-mount of the 6 real accounts is the user's (meltdown rail).

**Adversarial review (27 confirmed) + fixes — fusekit v0.20.0 + cc-pool main pushed @ 711acec0 (2026-06-26).** The 5-lens review (multi-tenant / bridge / data-integrity / probe / capability / cruft) found and the team fixed: **(A, hazard)** a transient content-bridge outage was misclassified `ErrMountFailed` → irreversible whole-pool symlink demotion (the cardinal "transient blip → the one irreversible action"); fixed in fusekit v0.20.0 with a retryable `mountd.ErrContentUnavailable` class (`mountErrClass` maps `content.ErrBridgeUnavailable`→it; Build still fails LOUD) + a 10s read deadline on the bridge handler, and cc-pool `healFuse` routes it to `healRetry`. **(B, HIGH functional)** several gates still used `fusekit.Built()` (always false on pure-Go) → `ccp fuse enable`/`migrate --to fuse` failed self-referentially, TCC note suppressed; all swapped to `pool.CanHostFuse()` (migrate.go/cli migrate/add/init). **(C)** the deleted Supervisor's pre-row ccp-add carcass clearing → restored as a bounded startup orphan-mountpoint sweep in `reconcileOverlays`. **(D)** ~31 stale comments referencing deleted `superviseHolder`/`Policy.Retreat`/`viewState`/revive-path/crash-loop → reconciled. Residual test-gap note: `pool.CanHostFuse()` stats `/Applications` so the gate sites' false-direction isn't reliably unit-testable without a new seam (pre-existing; codebase uses the `fuseGateFn` seam). NOTE: fusekit v0.19.0 took the overlay content-Setup; v0.20.0 took the bridge fix — so Phase 4A (cc-notes handle-token wire) is now v0.21.0+.

**Blocker for the cask (not the library):** `release.yml` fails at "Import Developer ID certificate" — the repo secrets `MACOS_SIGN_P12` / `MACOS_SIGN_PASSWORD` / `MACOS_NOTARY_KEY`/`_KEY_ID`/`_ISSUER_ID` / `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` are not configured. Until the user adds them, the signed `fusekit-holder` cask does not publish. The **go-module tag v0.18.0 is valid** (cc-pool/cc-notes consume the library on darwin, unaffected). 3B code + local testing use the dev path (`proc.Spawn.ExecPath` direct-exec to a locally-built holder); the cask `open -g` path is only needed for the production single-TCC-grant cutover (4C gate).

**3C.0 SHIPPED + LIVE CUTOVER 3C.1 ATTEMPTED (2026-06-27) — BLOCKED by 3 real bugs the live run surfaced; v0.35.0 NOT shippable.** 3C.0 (drop the dead `-tags fuse` build variant from release.yml + the `CGOFUSE_LIBFUSE_PATH` daemon env in service.go; pure-Go only) landed on `main @ b7698bdb`, all gates green. Then ran the live cutover on the user's Mac: `brew install --cask fusekit-holder` (v0.20.0) + `brew install --HEAD cc-pool` → daemon upgraded v0.34.0 → HEAD-b7698bd (running clean, content bridge bound). **Reality differed from the plan: all 6 accounts were persisted `overlay_kind=symlink`** — the old in-process holder CRASHED Jun 24 (panic dump in `~/.cc-pool/mount-holder.log`) and the heal-net retreated + persisted symlink; the user's been on degraded symlink (recurring acct-01 `mcp-needs-auth-cache.json` link conflict) 3 days. So the cutover = restore fuse via the cask holder, not move-fuse-accounts. **fuse-t is HEALTHY** (NFS backend go-nfsv4 1.2.7, NFSv4, mounts fine; `FskitSrvModule` is just a loaded component — NOT the active backend; my earlier FSKit-mismatch theory was WRONG). `ccp migrate --to fuse --account 1 --force` failed; root causes (system left CLEAN — every mount rolled back, nothing wedged, no meltdown):
1. **BLOCKER — fusekit holderfs: absent private-prefix backing breaks mount-come-up.** fuse-t.log shows the mount issues then `Lookup() of {1 0}/.credentials.json failed` → 8s `ErrMountTimeout` → rollback. `.credentials.json` is a `PrivatePrefix` ([[claude-pool-keychain-derivation]]: pool accounts auth via Keychain, NOT a file). It EXISTS in base `~/.claude/.credentials.json` (471B) so the holder lists it, but redirects to the account's `<accountDir>.private/.credentials.json` (`FusePrivateRoot` = accountDir+".private") which is ABSENT → `Lookup`/`Getattr` errors → stalls the NFS mount establishment. **Fix (fusekit holderfs.go Getattr/Lookup/Readdir):** an absent private-prefix backing must resolve as a clean ENOENT + NOT be listed — which is ALSO the cardinal safety behavior (a pool account must NEVER see plain claude's `.credentials.json`; see [[claude-pool-keychain-derivation]]). Unit-tested symlink path + the synth `.claude.json` never caught this because only a real fuse mount of a base that HAS `.credentials.json` exercises it.
2. **Daemon holder-spawn (direct-exec) fails for the CASK app.** `mountd`'s `proc.Spawn` direct-execs `mountd.HolderExe` (the cask's inner Mach-O); the launchd-daemon-spawned child "did not come up within 5s" with no log. Quarantine (`xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine`) did NOT fix it. Workaround that DID work: launch the holder via `open -g /Applications/fusekit-holder.app` (LaunchServices → ppid=1, proper responsible-process). **The production launch must be `open -g` or a cask LaunchAgent, NOT daemon direct-exec** — ties into [[fusekit-global-holder-direction]] (holder as its own launchd daemon). (TCC attribution turned out NOT to be the mount blocker — both Terminal- and LaunchServices-launched holders failed identically at the `.credentials.json` Lookup; the grant was already "proven".)
3. **`~/.fusekit/` socket dir not created by anyone.** `mountd.DefaultHolderSocket()` = `~/.fusekit/holder.sock` but nothing mkdirs `~/.fusekit` → bind ENOENT. **Fix:** the holder (or mountd spawn) must mkdir the socket parent.

Live state left: daemon HEAD-b7698bd on all-symlink (fork-bomb in-process-holder code GONE — the real safety win landed), cask installed + de-quarantined, `~/.fusekit` created (empty), no mounts, no stray holder. **cc-pool v0.35.0 must NOT tag until bugs #1+#2 are fixed + fuse re-validated** (else fuse users silently fall back to symlink). Fix order: fusekit holderfs ENOENT-for-absent-private (#1) + holder-launch-via-open-g/LaunchAgent (#2) + mkdir (#3) → release fusekit → rebuild cc-pool → re-validate acct-01 → roll all 6 → tag.

**FULL LIVE RE-FUSE COMPLETE 2026-07-02 (daemon HEAD-d11bafc).** All 6 accounts are now `overlay: nfs` on the mitigated v0.25.0 cask holder, ZERO kernel panic ([[macos-nfs-vinvalbuf2-panic]] validated live), 46/46 sessions survived. It required two cc-pool fixes surfaced during the forced re-fuse:
- **v0.36.1 — `mcp-needs-auth-cache.json` classified PRIVATE** (`internal/overlay/classify.go`, mirrors `remote-settings.json` in BOTH `PrivateEntry` + `PrivatePrefixes`). It was UNCLASSIFIED→shared→symlinked; claude rewrites it atomically (temp+rename) → clobbered the symlink into a real per-account file (drifted on acct-02/04). Unfixed, `convertToFuse`'s `MovePrivateEntries` (moves only private entries) would SHADOW the real file under the mount → silent revert to `~/.claude`'s shared copy, no error. Now moved into the per-account private root, content preserved.
- **v0.36.2 — convert post-mount identity verify reads the BACKING file, not through the mount** (`convert.go`: `readIdentity(filepath.Join(priv, ".claude.json"))`). The old through-mount `os.ReadFile` was UNBOUNDED and stalled at the macOS-NFS/fuse-t TRANSPORT layer whenever `ccp migrate --to fuse --force` converted a dir a live claude session still held (NOT a daemon lock — the bridge is concurrent, holder synth reads never park). It hung the migrate ~2min past the client 150s timeout, then rolled back onto the busy mount (graceful unmount fails) → stranded the account MOUNTED with row=symlink. Reproduced live on acct-01/02 before the fix; after the fix each account converts in ~0.3s. The mirror serves that exact backing file (ReadSynth), `oauthAccount` is blacklisted from the merge, so the identity check is value-identical; mount liveness stays covered by Setup's bounded MountAlive + mitigationGate health + heal loop.

**2026-07-03: fleet grown to 10 accounts, all re-fused onto nfs (~02:44).** The cutover surfaced
the holder-saturation incident — Darwin BG band on the holder tree + silly-rename privacy leak —
diagnosed and fixed in fusekit v0.27.0/v0.28.0: see [[holder-bg-band-incident]].

**Recovery gotchas learned (durable):** (a) a symlink-row live mount is NEVER adopted to nfs at runtime — the daemon only adopts fuse-row mounts at STARTUP; a stuck conversion's detached WithoutCancel goroutine may self-reconcile later (acct-01 did, logging `overlay migrated symlink -> nfs`). (b) `ccp migrate --to symlink --account N` is a NO-OP when the row already says symlink (`from==to` short-circuit). (c) force-unmounting a BUSY nfs mount panics the kernel — the symlink-retreat teardown is graceful-only, so a busy retreat fails clean (no-op). (d) `--force` under live sessions leaves every pre-existing session bound to a YANKED mount (`ccp doctor` flags "predates the current mirror — relaunch it"); sessions survive but must be relaunched to bind the new mirror. (e) symlink-origin accounts (no drifted real file) get an EMPTY mcp-cache backing → claude re-runs MCP auth once (benign; shared `~/.claude` copy untouched). Carried-forward: R7 (cc-notes onboards the shared holder), R8 (docs).
